structured.title: Seal oil pressure drop on Pump Skid PS-105B — mechanical seal leak probable
structured.summary: Seal oil differential pressure on PS-105B has dropped 22% over 48 hours from 3.8 bar to 2.96 bar. Process fluid traces detected in the seal oil return. Pattern is consistent with Stage 1 mechanical seal face wear. No temperature anomaly detected on the pump body, suggesting the leak is slow and containable if addressed within the current maintenance window.
hypothesis: Primary mechanical seal face wear on PS-105B is allowing process fluid to migrate into the seal oil circuit, causing progressive pressure loss.
Seal face carbon buildup from suspended solids in the process stream may be accelerating wear beyond the expected 18-month seal life.
root_causes: Mechanical seal face wear on the inboard seal of PS-105B
Possible contamination-accelerated wear from suspended solids in process fluid
contributing_factors: Pump has been operating at 108% of design flow for 3 weeks during a throughput surge
Last seal replacement was 16 months ago — approaching the 18-month expected life
immediate_actions: Increase seal oil monitoring frequency to every 2 hours until maintenance window
Confirm standby pump PS-105C is ready for immediate switchover if pressure drops below 2.5 bar
Notify operations of potential pump swap requirement within 48-72 hours
pm_suggestions: Create planned work order for PS-105B mechanical seal replacement during the next scheduled pump swap window
Order replacement seal cartridge and verify spare availability in warehouse
Add seal oil differential pressure to the high-frequency monitoring list for all PS-105 series pumps
